title: test-0040-MAT-CONSTRUCTIONS
passage: Teacher: Today, let us refine our geometry skills. Remember, a line segment has a fixed length, while a line extends infinitely. When measuring a segment starting at the 1 cm mark and ending at the 6 cm mark, you must subtract the start from the end to get 5 cm. Rahul: I am confused about triangles. Can I build one with sides 3 cm, 4 cm, and 7 cm? Teacher: No, Rahul. The sum of any two sides must be strictly greater than the third side. Here, 3 plus 4 equals 7, so they cannot meet to form a triangle. Priya: What about constructing a perpendicular bisector? Can I use any compass opening? Teacher: You must use a radius greater than half the segment length to ensure the arcs intersect. Also, remember that a perpendicular bisector is not just any line through the midpoint; it must be at a 90-degree angle. Finally, to construct a triangle using SAS, the angle must be placed exactly between the two given sides. If you place it elsewhere, you are not following the SAS rule. Always check your steps carefully to ensure your constructions are geometrically accurate and follow these fundamental rules.
summary: The sum of any two sides is always more than the third side. To construct a triangle using SAS, the angle must be placed exactly between the two given sides.
